messages.subject: .tps file formatting for geomorph readland.tps function
parts:
Hello Geomorph discussion group, 

I am a new user of geomorph with some basic questions I am hoping to have answered here, as my searches elsewhere online have not been very fruitful. 

I am conducting shape analyses on microCT scanned fossil primate teeth for my dissertation. I initially planned to use only fixed landmarks, but after some preliminary results, I have come to the conclusion that incorporating semi landmarks will better capture the shape variation that I am interested in.

With that, I am attempting to format my .tps file correctly so the readland.tps function will work. I am using SlicerMorph in 3DSlicer to digitize landmarks, which are saved separately as a .fcsv from the fixed landmarks. I have seen 2D .tps files that simply append how many curves are present in the specimen after the fixed landmarks and then list the coordinates of those points, but I cannot find any examples of this with 3D data. 

I am wondering, can someone please clarify the .tps file format for 3D data that is required for the readland.tps function?  Or please share an example? 

Many thanks in advance for fielding my basic questions, I hope this is an appropriate question to pose here! 
-Kathleen

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] .tps file formatting for geomorph readland.tps function
parts:
Kathleen,


There are several ways you can go. One is to read the .fcsv files into geomorph directly using the “readland.fcsv” function.

 

Alternatively, one can read in data as TPS, NTS, CSV or as a data table. Then, one can simply specify which landmarks are fixed, which are semilandmarks on curves, and which (for 3D data) are semilandmarks on surfaces. To identify the curve points, one creates a ‘slider’ matrix, which specifies which points are curve points, and which points they slide in between. Surface points are just identified by a vector of numbers.

 

If you look at the help file for gpagen (i.e., type ?gpagen) you will see descriptions of how these are provided to gpagen for Procrustes analysis. Also, at the bottom there are examples. The ‘hummingbirds’ dataset has 2D data with fixed points and curvepoints (meaning it also has the ‘slider matrix’). The 3D example ‘scallops’ has fixed points, curves, and surfaces and the various components specified.

 

These should be helpful as you work up your dataset in R and in geomorph.

 

Best,

 

Dean

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] .tps file formatting for geomorph readland.tps function
parts:
Kathleen,

Since you are doing your data collection via Slicer/SlicerMorph, you can also run your dataset using SlicerMorph GPAs module. There are two benefits to that:
1. If you have any digitization issues, or other sources of non-biological variation in data, you can discover those before running a full shape analysis (and pretty much fix immediately)
2. Importing data into geomorph becomes easier.

Instead of looping over individual FCSV (or JSON) files, you can use the parser function in the SlicerMorphR package to the log file SlicerMorph's GPA analysis produces. The $LM object of the returned variable will contain the fullset of specimens (and landmarks) that you included in the GPA. You can pass that object to gpagen() and do your sliding....

You can install the SlicerMorphR with the devtools: devtools::install_github('SlicerMorph/SlicerMorphR')

and then see a worked example: https://github.com/SlicerMorph/Tutorials/blob/main/GPA_3/parser_and_sample_R_analysis.md

parts: Ps. The sooner you make the transition, the fewer datasets you will have that you have to worry about later.

Hi Kathleen,

I think the issue is simple. 

Only newer version of the SLicerMorph's GPA module outputs the log file in in JSON format. You have the older .log file format and trying to use the new parser (parser2) that expects JSON as input. 

Please use the parser() function instead of parser2(), and see if resolves the issue.

Only newer version of the SLicerMorph's GPA module outputs the log file in in JSON format. You have the older .log file format and trying to use the new parser (parser2) that expects JSON as input. 

Please use the parser() function instead of parser2(), and see if resolves the issue.

On Wednesday, May 29, 2024 at 5:27:29 PM UTC-5 mura...@gmail.com wrote:
Kathleen,

Since you are doing your data collection via Slicer/SlicerMorph, you can also run your dataset using SlicerMorph GPAs module. There are two benefits to that:
1. If you have any digitization issues, or other sources of non-biological variation in data, you can discover those before running a full shape analysis (and pretty much fix immediately)
2. Importing data into geomorph becomes easier.

Instead of looping over individual FCSV (or JSON) files, you can use the parser function in the SlicerMorphR package to the log file SlicerMorph's GPA analysis produces. The $LM object of the returned variable will contain the fullset of specimens (and landmarks) that you included in the GPA. You can pass that object to gpagen() and do your sliding....

You can install the SlicerMorphR with the devtools: devtools::install_github('SlicerMorph/SlicerMorphR')

and then see a worked example: https://github.com/SlicerMorph/Tutorials/blob/main/GPA_3/parser_and_sample_R_analysis.md



On Wednesday, May 29, 2024 at 12:38:57 PM UTC-7 dca...@iastate.edu wrote:

Kathleen,


There are several ways you can go. One is to read the .fcsv files into geomorph directly using the “readland.fcsv” function.

 

Alternatively, one can read in data as TPS, NTS, CSV or as a data table. Then, one can simply specify which landmarks are fixed, which are semilandmarks on curves, and which (for 3D data) are semilandmarks on surfaces. To identify the curve points, one creates a ‘slider’ matrix, which specifies which points are curve points, and which points they slide in between. Surface points are just identified by a vector of numbers.

 

If you look at the help file for gpagen (i.e., type ?gpagen) you will see descriptions of how these are provided to gpagen for Procrustes analysis. Also, at the bottom there are examples. The ‘hummingbirds’ dataset has 2D data with fixed points and curvepoints (meaning it also has the ‘slider matrix’). The 3D example ‘scallops’ has fixed points, curves, and surfaces and the various components specified.

 

These should be helpful as you work up your dataset in R and in geomorph.

 

Best,

 

Dean

I am using SlicerMorph in 3DSlicer to digitize landmarks, which are saved separately as a .fcsv from the fixed landmarks. I have seen 2D .tps files that simply append how many curves are present in the specimen after the fixed landmarks and then list the coordinates of those points, but I cannot find any examples of this with 3D data. 

 

I am wondering, can someone please clarify the .tps file format for 3D data that is required for the readland.tps function?  Or please share an example? 

 

Many thanks in advance for fielding my basic questions, I hope this is an appropriate question to pose here! 

-Kathleen
